note: D6 defines 40 new NFR ids and cites 6 from earlier units; high-water marks were recomputed across the whole aidlc tree before numbering, zero collisions verified. The unit adds NO library, service or tool - everything it needs is built, which is what a terminal spec unit should look like. NFR14.83 is the strongest requirement here and is new to the project: a test over the LIVE foreign-key constraints asserting no CASCADE to account.id exists against a RETAIN_WITH_BASIS table, which fails on a newly added contradicting constraint before anyone deletes anything; NFR14.99 makes that reachability TRANSITIVE after review found depth-one missed the owner -> batch chain entirely. Status counts, derived from the rows rather than stated: 32 OK, 6 N/A, 2 Deferred, zero GAP. Five ids were added after review: NFR14.98 (a sign-in code would confirm a deletion as built), NFR14.99 (transitive reachability), NFR14.100 (deletion needs its own number-scoped counter or an attacker locks victims out of signing in), NFR14.101 (the manifest basis must be corrected, not only the disposition), NFR14.102 (a deletion-specific GLOBAL sub-ceiling, because the per-IP and per-number ceilings bind neither a botnet nor a many-numbers-once-each attack).

construction/releasing-safely/nfr-requirements/security-requirements.md section 1 - a deletion code is its own PURPOSE. As built, issue() takes no purpose argument and verify() does not filter on one, so a SIGN-IN code would confirm a DELETION. OTP_PURPOSE own docstring predicted this: a DEFAULT would let a second consumer arrive without anyone choosing its ceiling. Verifier: issue a sign-in code, present it to the deletion confirmation, assert refusal

construction/releasing-safely/nfr-requirements/security-requirements.md section 2 - the cascade reachability is computed TRANSITIVELY, not depth-one. Written and run against the live schema: the recursive query finds ELEVEN RETAIN_WITH_BASIS tables, seven of them reachable only through owner -> batch, which 0007 does not touch. This settles that BR1.6 refusal is LOAD-BEARING rather than belt-and-braces; 0007 alone would leave a teacher deletion destroying seven kinds of retained record. The path column is the diagnostic

construction/releasing-safely/nfr-requirements/security-requirements.md section 1 - deletion gets its OWN ceiling scopes, not the sign-in budget. PER_NUMBER limits count per NUMBER not per requester, so an attacker with a number list can spend each victim daily allowance from the public page and lock them out of signing in without deleting anything. Signup has SIGNUP_NUMBER_DAILY for exactly this reason. Verifier: exhaust the deletion scope, assert a SIGN-IN code still issues for the same number

construction/releasing-safely/nfr-requirements/security-requirements.md section 4 - the account entry disposition AND its basis are both corrected. The generator reads the basis field and NFR14.89 asserts a disclosure is PRESENT; neither catches a basis that is merely WRONG, so without this the policy would faithfully publish an argument the schema no longer supports. A generated document is only as true as the field it reads

construction/releasing-safely/nfr-requirements/security-requirements.md section 1 - deletion carries its own GLOBAL daily sub-ceiling (50 carved out of 500), because the other two ceilings do not bind a botnet: ip_prefix_of reduces a caller to a /24 so spanning prefixes never meets PER_IP_HOURLY, and many-numbers-once-each never meets a per-number limit. That leaves GLOBAL_DAILY as the only bound and it is GLOBAL, so draining it from an unauthenticated page denies SIGN-IN to every legitimate user for the day. Human decision 2026-10-25. Verifier: drain the deletion sub-ceiling, assert a sign-in code still issues
